chunks: And Sulaymān ibn Dāwūd al-Minqarī narrated from Ḥafṣ ibn Ghiyāth, who said:
I heard Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام say:

Regarding a man who caught the Jumuʿah prayer while the people had become crowded: he said the takbīr with the Imam and performed rukuʿ, but was unable to perform sajdah. Then the Imam and the people rose for the second rakʿah, and this man rose with them. Then the Imam performed rukuʿ, but this man was unable to perform rukuʿ in the second rakʿah because of the crowding, while he was able to perform sajdah. How should he act?

He عليه السلام said: "As for the first rakʿah, it is complete up to the point of rukuʿ. Since he did not perform sajdah for it until he entered the second rakʿah, that was not valid for him. Then, when he performed sajdah in the second, if he had intended these two sajdahs for the first rakʿah, then the first is complete for him. So when the Imam gives taslīm, he stands and prays one rakʿah, performs sajdah in it, then recites the tashahhud and gives taslīm. But if he had not intended the two sajdahs for the first rakʿah, then neither the first nor the second counts for him, and he must perform two sajdahs while intending that they are for the first rakʿah, and after that he owes one complete rakʿah in which he performs sajdah."

key_terms.الزِّحَامِ: crowding that physically prevents completing the prayer movements
key_terms.السَّجْدَتَيْنِ: the two prostrations belonging to a rakʿah
key_terms.الْإِمَامِ: the prayer leader being followed in congregation
key_terms.نَوَى: he intended; formed the required niyyah (intention)

ai.seo_question: How should someone complete Jumuʿah prayer if crowding prevents him from performing rukuʿ or sajdah with the Imam?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling for a person who joins Jumuʿah prayer in severe crowding and cannot complete the normal sequence of rukuʿ and sajdah. It explains how intention and the order of actions affect whether the rakʿah is counted, and how the worshipper should complete the prayer after the Imam's taslīm.
